answer: An agent economy resists sybils by making every identity earn its ledge of trust layer by layer, like shale: a new agent must post a refundable bond and complete verifiable work before it can transact, and each finished job adds one thin, attested layer to its reputation. To forge a fake identity an attacker must pay the same bond and do the same work for every single copy, with no shortcut to a thick reputation, so a thousand fakes cost a thousand bonds and a thousand jobs, while one honest agent pays once and keeps earning.
